privacy.metaDescription: How TejoTime collects, uses, shares, and protects information across our website, booking pages, and owner app.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: TejoTime is operated by {entity}. This Privacy Policy explains how {entity} (“TejoTime,” “we,” “us”) collects, uses, shares, and protects information when you use our website, our owner and staff apps, and the public booking pages we host for businesses. Please read it alongside our Terms of Service.

sections.heading: 1. Who uses TejoTime, and who controls your data
paragraphs: TejoTime serves two groups of people, and the role we play is different for each.

Business users are the salons, barbershops, nail studios, spas, med spas, massage practices, physical therapy clinics, tattoo studios, and pet-grooming businesses that sign up for an account. For information about a business user’s own account, we act as the controller of that information and this policy applies directly.

Clients of those businesses are the people who book an appointment or join a walk-in waitlist through a business’s TejoTime booking page. For that information, the business is the controller and TejoTime acts as a service provider processing information on that business’s instructions. If you are a client and want your information corrected or deleted, contact the business you booked with first; we will support that business in responding.
TejoTime is a tool for businesses. It is not directed at children under 13.

sections.heading: 2. Information we collect
paragraphs: We collect the following categories of information:
For a full list of the cookies we set, what each one does, and how to change your choices at any time, see our Cookie Policy at /cookies.
bullets: Account information — the phone number and password used to sign in, plus the name, role, and business details you enter when you create or join a business account.
Business content — your business name, address, hours, services, prices, photos, staff names and photos, and anything else you publish to your booking page.
Client records you add — client names, phone numbers, appointment and visit history, preferences, and any notes you or your team choose to record.
Booking information from clients — the name, phone number, service, and appointment or waitlist details a client provides when they book through a business’s booking page.
Device and technical information — sign-in tokens stored securely on your device, app or browser version, and the basic device and network information needed to operate and secure the service.
Photos you choose to upload — we access your photo library only at the moment you pick an image. We never access your camera or photo library in the background.
Support communications — the contents of emails and messages you send us.

sections.heading: 3. What we do not collect
paragraphs: We do not collect precise GPS location, your device contacts, or your SMS messages.

We do not collect or store payment card numbers. TejoTime does not process payments for appointments; clients pay the business directly. If we introduce paid subscription billing, payment details will be handled by a third-party payment processor and this policy will be updated before that happens.

sections.heading: 4. How we use information
paragraphs: We use the information described above to:
bullets: Create your account and sign you in securely.
Operate your calendar, appointments, optional walk-in waitlist, and client records.
Publish and serve your public booking page.
Send booking confirmations, appointment reminders, and operational messages about your business or booking.
Provide customer support and help set up your account during the U.S. pilot.
Maintain, troubleshoot, secure, and improve the service, and prevent fraud and abuse.
Comply with legal obligations and enforce our Terms of Service.

sections.heading: 5. Text messages (SMS) and email
paragraphs: Where enabled for a business, TejoTime sends up to three kinds of text message, each tied to a specific visit: a confirmation when you book an appointment, a reminder 15 minutes before it starts, and one message after your visit asking you to leave the business a review. We do not send recurring texts or any other promotional texts.

You opt in by checking the one optional, unchecked-by-default SMS box on a business’s TejoTime page when you book an appointment or check in. That box covers all three messages, and we only text your number if it is checked. You can finish a booking or check-in without agreeing to any texts.
Message frequency: up to 3 messages per visit. Message and data rates may apply.

Reply STOP to any message to stop receiving texts from TejoTime, or ask the business to remove you. Reply HELP, or contact us at {email} or {phone}, for help. Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages.
We do not sell or share your SMS opt-in data or personal information with third parties for marketing purposes.

We do not sell, rent, or share your mobile phone number or your text-message opt-in status with third parties or affiliates for their own marketing or promotional purposes. Text messaging originator opt-in data and consent will not be shared with any third parties. Businesses are responsible for having an appropriate basis to contact their own clients.

sections.heading: 6. How we share information
paragraphs: We do not sell personal information, and we do not share personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising. We share information only in these situations:
bullets: Service providers — hosting, database, file storage, email, and messaging providers that operate the service on our behalf under written contracts limiting their use of the information.
People you invite — staff and providers you add to your business account can see the business content and client records their role allows.
Your published booking page — the business name, address, hours, services, prices, photos, and staff you choose to publish are public by design.
Legal reasons — when required by law, subpoena, or to protect the rights, safety, or property of TejoTime, our users, or the public.

Business transfers — if TejoTime is involved in a merger, acquisition, or sale of assets, information may transfer as part of that transaction; we will notify you before your information becomes subject to a different policy.

sections.heading: 7. How long we keep information
paragraphs: We keep account and business data for as long as the account is active. You can ask us to delete a business account or your personal account by emailing {email}.

After a deletion request we remove or de-identify the data within a reasonable period, except where we must keep records to comply with law, resolve disputes, or enforce our agreements. Backups are purged on a rolling schedule.

sections.heading: 8. Security
paragraphs: Passwords are stored using one-way hashing. Session tokens are held in the device secure store. Data is transmitted over encrypted connections, and access to production systems is limited to personnel who need it.

No method of transmission or storage is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security. If we become aware of a breach affecting your information, we will notify you as required by applicable law.

sections.heading: 9. Your privacy rights
paragraphs: Depending on where you live, you may have the right to request access to the personal information we hold about you, request that we correct it, request that we delete it, request a portable copy, and appeal a decision we make about your request. Residents of California, Colorado, Connecticut, Virginia, and other states with comprehensive privacy laws have these rights under those laws.
Because we do not sell personal information or share it for cross-context behavioral advertising, there is nothing to opt out of in those categories.

To exercise a right, email {email} from the address or phone number associated with your account. We will verify your request before acting on it, and we will not discriminate against you for making one. If you are a client of a business that uses TejoTime, send your request to that business and we will assist them.

sections.heading: 10. Responsibilities of businesses using TejoTime
paragraphs: If you use TejoTime to run your business, you are responsible for the client information you enter and for having an appropriate basis to collect and store it. That includes client notes and any photographs you upload.

TejoTime is a scheduling and client-management tool. It is not designed or offered as a system for storing medical records, insurance information, or other regulated health data, and it should not be used for that purpose.

sections.heading: 11. Children’s privacy
paragraphs: TejoTime is intended for business users and their adult clients. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. If you believe a child has provided us information, email {email} and we will delete it.
Where a business books appointments for a minor, the business is responsible for obtaining any consent required from a parent or guardian.

sections.heading: 12. Where your information is processed
paragraphs: TejoTime is operated for the United States market, and information may be stored and processed in the United States and in other countries where our service providers operate. Those countries may have different data protection rules than your own. We use contractual protections with our providers to safeguard information wherever it is processed.

sections.heading: 13. Changes to this policy
paragraphs: We may update this policy from time to time. When we do, we will revise the “Last updated” date above, and we will provide additional notice for material changes. Continuing to use TejoTime after an update means you accept the revised policy.

sections.heading: 14. Contact us
paragraphs: Questions about this policy or about how your information is handled? Contact us using the details below and we will respond within a reasonable period.

terms.metaDescription: The terms that govern your use of TejoTime’s online booking, scheduling, and client-management service.
terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: TejoTime is operated by {entity}. These Terms of Service (“Terms”) are an agreement between you and {entity} (“TejoTime,” “we,” “us”). They govern your use of our website, our owner and staff apps, and the booking pages we host. By creating an account or using TejoTime, you agree to these Terms. If you do not agree, do not use the service.

sections.heading: 1. Who may use TejoTime
paragraphs: You must be at least 18 years old to create an account. If you are accepting these Terms for a business, you represent that you have authority to bind that business, and “you” refers to both you and that business.
TejoTime is offered for business use in the United States. You are responsible for complying with the laws and licensing requirements that apply to your business.

sections.heading: 2. Your account
paragraphs: You sign in with a phone number and a password. You are responsible for keeping your credentials confidential and for all activity under your account.

You may invite staff and providers to your business account. You are responsible for the access you grant them, for removing access when someone leaves, and for their use of the service. Notify us at {email} promptly if you believe your account has been compromised.

sections.heading: 3. The U.S. pilot
paragraphs: TejoTime is currently offered through a United States pilot program. During the pilot we help you set up your services, schedule, and booking page. The Starter plan is free for the first month, then $9.99/month as published on our website.

Pilot features may change, and the pilot may end. We will give you reasonable advance notice before the pilot ends or before any change to the published price that applies to your plan. Pilot participation does not guarantee any particular future price.

sections.heading: 4. Plans, pricing, and billing
paragraphs: Pricing for paid plans will be published on our website before those plans become chargeable. We will not charge you for a paid plan without your express agreement to the price and billing terms in effect at that time.

When paid plans launch, subscription fees will be billed in advance for the applicable term, fees are exclusive of taxes, and you authorize us and our payment processor to charge your selected payment method. Unless a plan states otherwise, subscriptions renew automatically until cancelled.

You may cancel your subscription at any time in accordance with the terms shown for your plan. Cancellation takes effect at the end of your current billing period, and you keep access until then. Except where required by law, fees already paid are not refundable.

sections.heading: 5. What TejoTime does and does not do
paragraphs: TejoTime provides scheduling, booking, reminder, and client-management software. We are not a party to the appointments you book or the services you provide, and we do not process payments for those services — your clients pay you directly.

You set your own services, prices, hours, deposits, cancellation rules, and no-show policies, and you are responsible for honoring and enforcing them. Estimated wait times shown on a walk-in waitlist are estimates only and are not a guarantee to you or to your clients.
TejoTime is not a medical records system. Do not use it to store medical records, insurance information, or other regulated health information.

sections.heading: 6. Your content
paragraphs: You keep ownership of the business information, photos, client records, and other content you put into TejoTime (“Your Content”).

accessibility.metaDescription: TejoTime’s accessibility commitment, current conformance status, known limitations, and how to report a barrier.
accessibility.title: Accessibility Statement
accessibility.intro: {entity} is committed to making TejoTime usable by as many people as possible, including people who use screen readers, keyboard navigation, magnification, or other assistive technology. This statement describes where we stand today, what we know is not finished, and how to tell us when something does not work.

sections.heading: 1. Our commitment
paragraphs: Booking an appointment should not depend on being able to see a screen, use a mouse, or read small text. We treat accessibility as part of building the product rather than as a later cleanup, and we take reported barriers seriously.
This commitment covers our marketing website, the public booking pages we host for businesses, and our owner and staff apps.

sections.heading: 2. Conformance status
paragraphs: We are working toward conformance with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at Level AA.

TejoTime is currently partially conformant with WCAG 2.1 Level AA. “Partially conformant” means that some parts of the content do not yet fully meet the standard. We have listed the gaps we know about in section 4 rather than claiming a level we have not verified.

sections.heading: 3. What we have implemented
paragraphs: The following are in place across our public pages today:
bullets: A declared page language, semantic headings, and landmark regions so screen readers can navigate structure.
Text that scales with browser and device settings — we do not lock zoom or set a maximum scale on mobile.
Reduced-motion support: animations and transitions are suppressed when your system requests reduced motion.
Accessible names on navigation, menu buttons, and interactive controls, including expanded and controlled-element state on the mobile menu.
Tab semantics on the product tour so it can be operated and announced as a tab set.
Decorative images marked so assistive technology can skip them.
Layouts built to reflow on small screens and at high zoom without horizontal scrolling.

sections.heading: 4. Known limitations
paragraphs: We are aware of the following and are working on them:
bullets: Visible focus indicators are not yet styled consistently across every custom control, which makes keyboard position harder to track in places.
There is no “skip to main content” link yet on the marketing pages.

Photographs, service descriptions, and business names are uploaded by the businesses that use TejoTime. We cannot guarantee that business-supplied images carry meaningful alternative text, and we are adding guidance and prompts to help owners provide it.
Some product demonstration areas on the homepage are illustrative and are being reviewed for full screen-reader parity with the underlying product.
Colour contrast is being audited across every theme variation rather than only the default one.

sections.heading: 5. Compatibility
paragraphs: TejoTime is designed to work with current versions of major browsers — Chrome, Safari, Edge, and Firefox — on desktop and mobile, used together with the assistive technology available on those platforms.
The site relies on JavaScript for some interactive areas. If you encounter a page that does not work with your setup, tell us and we will help you complete what you were trying to do.

sections.heading: 6. Technical specifications
paragraphs: Accessibility of TejoTime relies on HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and WAI-ARIA, and on the combination of those technologies with the browser and assistive technology installed on your device.

sections.heading: 7. How we assess accessibility
paragraphs: Our current assessment is a self-evaluation carried out by our own team using automated checks and manual keyboard and screen-reader testing.
We have not yet commissioned an independent third-party audit. When we do, we will update this statement with the date and scope of that review.

sections.heading: 8. Feedback and requests
paragraphs: If you run into a barrier on any TejoTime page, we want to know. Email {email} and, where you can, include the page address, what you were trying to do, and the browser and assistive technology you were using.
We aim to acknowledge accessibility reports within five business days. If a fix will take longer, we will tell you what we are doing and offer another way to complete your task in the meantime.
If you need to book an appointment and the booking page is not working for you, contact the business directly — their phone number and address are listed on their TejoTime page.

sections.heading: 9. Escalation
paragraphs: If you are not satisfied with our response, reply to our email and ask for the report to be escalated. We will review it again and respond with our conclusion.
This statement will be reviewed and updated as we address the limitations listed above.

cookies.title: Cookie Policy
cookies.intro: This Cookie Policy explains which cookies and similar technologies {entity} uses on tejotime.com and on the public booking pages we host, what each one is for, and how you can change your choices. Read it alongside our Privacy Policy.

sections.heading: 1. What cookies are
paragraphs: A cookie is a small text file a website stores in your browser. It lets a site remember something between page loads — for example that you already chose your cookie preferences, or that you are signed in.

Some technologies are not cookies but do a similar job. Our public booking pages use your browser's local storage to remember your place in a queue. We treat that the same way we treat a necessary cookie, and it is listed below.

sections.heading: 2. What TejoTime actually uses today
paragraphs: We want to be precise here, because a cookie policy that lists cookies a site does not set is misleading.

TejoTime currently sets NO analytics cookies and NO marketing or advertising cookies. There is no Google Analytics, no advertising pixel, and no third-party tracker on this website. The Analytics and Marketing categories appear in your cookie settings so that your choice is already recorded and respected if we ever introduce them — until then, leaving them on changes nothing and sets nothing.
Every cookie below is a first-party cookie, meaning it is set by TejoTime and not by an outside company. We do not sell or share personal information with third parties for advertising.

sections.heading: 3. The cookies we use
paragraphs: cookie_consent — Stores your cookie choices and a random identifier for that record, so we can prove what you agreed to and not ask you again on every page. Category: Necessary. Duration: 6 months. First party.

tt_owner_at and tt_owner_rt — Keep a business owner or staff member signed in to the owner portal at business.tejotime.com. These are set when signing in there, not by this website. Category: Necessary. Duration: about 15 minutes and 30 days. First party.
tt_admin_session — Keeps a TejoTime staff member signed in to our internal admin panel. Set only on that panel, not by this website. Category: Necessary. Duration: about 12 hours. First party.

Booking page local storage — On a business's public booking page, your browser stores your current queue ticket so you can close the tab and still return to your place in line. Category: Necessary and functional. Duration: until you leave the queue or clear your browser data. First party.

sections.heading: 4. What the categories mean
paragraphs: Your cookie settings group everything into four categories.
bullets: Necessary — Required for the site to work at all: remembering your cookie choice, keeping you signed in, and holding your place in a queue. These cannot be switched off, because switching them off would break the thing you came to do.
Analytics — Would tell us which pages people use and where they get stuck, so we can improve them. Nothing in this category is in use today.
Marketing — Would measure advertising and show more relevant ads. Nothing in this category is in use today.
Preferences — Would remember choices such as language or region to personalise your visit. Nothing in this category is in use today.

sections.heading: 5. How to change your choices
paragraphs: Select Cookie Settings in the footer of any page to reopen the preferences panel and change any optional category. Your change takes effect immediately.
If you withdraw consent for a category you previously allowed, we stop using it straight away and remove any cookies that category had set.
You can also block or delete cookies in your browser settings. Blocking necessary cookies will stop parts of the site working — you may be signed out, or lose your place in a queue.

sections.heading: 6. How long your choice is kept
paragraphs: Your cookie choice is stored for 6 months, after which we ask again. We will also ask again sooner if we change what the categories cover, so your consent always matches what we actually do.

We keep a record of each choice — the random identifier from your cookie, which categories you allowed, the policy version, the time, and the country your request came from — so that we can demonstrate consent if asked. We do not store your IP address or your browser's user agent with it.

sections.heading: 7. More information
paragraphs: Our Privacy Policy at /privacy explains what personal information we collect and your rights over it, including how to request access or deletion. If you have a question about this policy, contact us using the details below.
